solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Very wet Liberal admitted being careless

indicators.note: something admitted is let inside, so the party letter goes within the other word

parts.note: soppy means soaked through, thoroughly wet
L is the standard abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: A drippy Liberal politician confesses to having been negligent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very wet' reads like a political jibe at a feeble Liberal, but it is simply SOPPY, with L let in: S(L)OPPY.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloppy work is slapdash, done without due care or attention, a straightforward synonym of careless.

clue.text: Work hard on article that can convey message briefly

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed after, so the article follows the word for work hard

parts.note: to slog is to work hard
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A copywriter toils over a newspaper piece meant to get its point across quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: A slogan is a short, memorable phrase used to put across an idea or advertisement, a message in brief.

clue.text: SF writer, one in series of books too precise?

indicators.note: in places the writer and the number inside the abbreviation for the collection

parts.note: the Old Testament is a series of books
Jules Verne, pioneer of science fiction
a means one

explanation.surface: Asks whether a science-fiction author in a book series is overly exact.
explanation.walkthrough: OT, the Old Testament, is a crossword staple for a series of books; Jules Verne is the classic SF writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Overneat means excessively tidy or exact; the question mark flags it as a fair but loose synonym of too precise.

clue.text: Holy person seen as unique sort of explorer once?

parts.note: pi is slang for pious, a holy person
a oner is something unique, one of a kind

explanation.surface: A saint is regarded as a one-off, an explorer of a bygone kind.
explanation.walkthrough: PI + ONER. 'Once' marks pioner as an obsolete spelling of pioneer.
explanation.definitionFit: Pioner is an old form of pioneer, one who goes first into new territory, a kind of explorer.

clue.text: Dear people of old posed with beam, having turned up

indicators.note: in a down entry turned up means read upwards, so the letters run in the opposite order

parts.note: to sit for a portrait is to pose
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: Old-fashioned darlings posed with a beam of light, once they had shown up.
explanation.walkthrough: SAT + RAY gives SATRAY, reversed in the down light. Yarta is an old Shetland word, a term of endearment.
explanation.definitionFit: Yarta is an obsolete Shetland endearment meaning heart or dear, so yartas are dear people of old.

clue.text: Aspects of truths about Earth

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word wraps around the abbreviation

parts.note: facts are truths
E is the abbreviation for Earth

explanation.surface: Sounds like a phrase from a science essay on different sides of the truth about our planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Facets are the separate sides or features of a subject, just as aspects are.

clue.text: Nest well ventilated in which eagle finally settles

indicators.note: in which means inside that word, so the letter settles within the word for airy
to settle is to come to rest somewhere, here inside the other word

parts.note: an airy room is well ventilated

indicators.note: finally points to the very end, so only the last letter of the bird is used

parts.note: the final letter of eagle

explanation.surface: An airy nest where an eagle finally makes its home.
explanation.walkthrough: Aiery is a variant spelling of eyrie, the word the definition first suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: An aiery or eyrie is the nest of a bird of prey, built high up.

clue.text: Argument against illegal trade group ignored

indicators.note: ignored means left out, so the word for group is removed from the longer word

parts.note: contraband is smuggled goods, or illicit trading
a band is a group

explanation.surface: A case against an illegal trading ring that was overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: CONTRABAND minus BAND.
explanation.definitionFit: A contra is a point on the opposing side of a debate, as in pros and contras.

clue.text: Little creatures are wandering around in cat hair possibly

indicators.note: wandering around suggests roaming in no fixed order, so the letters move about
possibly hints that these letters might form something else, a rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Tiny creatures roaming through a cat's fur, fleas perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of are and cat hair are combined and rearranged. Trachearia are arachnids, such as mites, that breathe by tracheae.
explanation.definitionFit: Trachearia is an old zoological grouping of small air-breathing arachnids, chiefly mites, hence little creatures.

clue.text: Spoke about old lover getting help in bed?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the verb wraps around the former partner

parts.note: said is the past tense of speak
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: Someone talked of a former partner who received assistance between the sheets.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark warns that 'help in bed' is meant playfully, not as nursing care.
explanation.definitionFit: A sex aid is a device or product meant to enhance sexual activity, so literally help in bed.

clue.text: Priest on channel not initially giving uplifting performance

indicators.note: not initially tells us to drop the opening letter of the word for channel

parts.note: a Levite or Levi is one of the priestly tribe of Israel; Levi is also a biblical priest's name
a TV or radio channel is a station

explanation.surface: A clergyman on television avoids giving an inspiring show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifting' reads as inspiring, but it is literal: a performance in which something rises.
explanation.definitionFit: Levitation, rising into the air, is a conjuror's trick, a performance that is literally uplifting.

clue.text: Small mammal, funny without tail, occupying fortress

indicators.note: occupying means sitting inside, so the shortened word is placed within the stronghold

parts.note: a castle is a fortress

indicators.note: without tail means losing the last letter of the word for funny

parts.note: comic means funny

explanation.surface: A tailless little animal that looks amusing has taken over a fort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without tail' attaches to funny, not to the mammal, even though the surface pictures a tailless creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The cacomistle is the ringtail, a small raccoon-like animal of Mexico and the south-western United States.

clue.text: Environmental levy welcome, new coming in — tool for USA?

indicators.note: coming in means entering, so the letter for new goes inside the word for welcome

parts.note: to greet is to welcome
N is the abbreviation for new
ax is the American spelling of the chopping tool axe

explanation.surface: A green levy is welcomed, a new one arriving, and asks whether it is a policy instrument for America.
explanation.walkthrough: GREE(N)T then AX; 'for USA' signals the American spelling without the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: A green tax is a charge imposed to protect the environment, such as a levy on pollution.

clue.text: Kangaroo or rhino on the Continent

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a large reddish kangaroo, the wallaroo
second meaning: rhino is British slang for money, and on the Continent money is this currency

explanation.surface: A puzzle about which exotic animal you might find in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rhino' looks like the animal, but it is old British slang for cash; the European currency is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a species of kangaroo and the shared currency of most European Union countries.

clue.text: Stone trap fish approaches

indicators.note: approaches means coming up to, so the fish comes just ahead of the trap

parts.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish
a net is a trap

explanation.surface: A stone-built fish trap with fish swimming towards it.
explanation.definitionFit: Garnet is a semi-precious gem, a stone often deep red in colour.

clue.text: Nettle that's hurt I can cut first and last

indicators.note: cut first and last says to remove the first letter of one word and the last of another

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone stung by a nettle says they can cut it down from top to bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: From 'hurt I can', hurt loses its first letter and can its last: URT + I + CA.
explanation.definitionFit: Urtica is the botanical genus name of the stinging nettles.

clue.text: Bill and Edmund suffering from skin complaint

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill
Ned is a pet form of Edmund
joins the two names

explanation.surface: Two men, Bill and Edmund, both have bad skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a name alongside Edmund, but it is an account, AC.
explanation.definitionFit: Acned means affected by acne, a skin complaint of spots and pimples.

clue.text: Couple entertaining heartless revolutionary outdoors

indicators.note: entertaining means having as a guest, so the word for couple holds the other inside

parts.note: a pair is a couple

indicators.note: heartless means with the centre removed, so the middle letter of the revolutionary goes

parts.note: Lenin led the Russian Revolution

explanation.surface: Two people host a callous revolutionary out in the open.
explanation.walkthrough: Plein air is French; the term came into English through the Impressionist painters.
explanation.definitionFit: Plein air, from the French for open air, describes painting done outdoors rather than in a studio.

clue.text: Pagan god generating fear, lots regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter of the phrase is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A heathen deity inspires much terror.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek god of love, a deity of the pre-Christian, pagan pantheon.

clue.text: Ring given wan appearance or made iridescent?

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
to pale is to become or make wan

explanation.surface: A ring that has gone dull, or perhaps one shimmering with colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Opaled means made opalescent, showing the shifting rainbow colours of an opal.

clue.text: A Greek character holding a party — such could get fired up

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: holding means keeping inside, so the Greek letter grips the party phrase

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
A plus DO, a party

explanation.surface: A Greek man hosting a party, which might get everyone fired up.
explanation.walkthrough: A + M(A DO)U. Amadou is tinder made from a bracket fungus, used for lighting fires.
explanation.definitionFit: Amadou is fungal tinder, so it is something that can be set alight, literally fired up.

clue.text: Humiliated when found participating in a plot

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: participating in means taking part within, so the word for when goes inside

parts.note: a flower bed is a plot of ground
as can mean when

explanation.surface: Someone was disgraced once caught taking part in a conspiracy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' suggests a conspiracy, but it is a garden plot, a BED: A B(AS)ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be abased is to be lowered in dignity, humbled or humiliated.

clue.text: Fraudulent behaviour of party truly in want of leader

indicators.note: in want of leader means lacking a first letter, so the word for truly loses its head

parts.note: the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland
very in its old sense of true, real

explanation.surface: A political party is accused of cheating while lacking a leader.
explanation.walkthrough: DUP then VERY without its V. The DUP is a Northern Irish political party.
explanation.definitionFit: Dupery is the practice of duping, deceiving or tricking people, hence fraudulent behaviour.

clue.text: Vessels of our navy protected by our people

indicators.note: protected by means shielded on both sides, so the navy sits inside the word for our people

parts.note: us means our group of people
RN is the Royal Navy, Britain's navy

explanation.surface: Ships of the national navy are defended by the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessels' with 'navy' suggests ships, but these are pots: U(RN)S.
explanation.definitionFit: Urns are vases or containers, vessels used for holding ashes or liquids.

clue.text: Youngster with energy — eight?

parts.note: a cub is a young animal, or a young scout
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A young person full of energy, perhaps aged eight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eight?' looks like the youngster's age; it is the number 8, which is 2 times 2 times 2.
explanation.definitionFit: Eight is a cube number, two raised to the third power; the question mark marks it as an example.

clue.text: Something biological that once would appear in secret message

indicators.note: appear in means show up inside, so the old word sits within the secret writing

parts.note: a code conceals a message
YT is an old written abbreviation of that, with Y standing for the old thorn letter

explanation.surface: Something from biology that used to crop up in a coded note.
explanation.walkthrough: Old manuscripts wrote 'that' with a y standing for the old letter thorn, hence 'that once'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cytode is a primitive cell without a nucleus, an entity studied in biology.

clue.text: No longer mention a maiden in prayer

indicators.note: in places one item inside the other, so the pair of letters goes into the prayer word

parts.note: bene is an archaic word for a prayer
A plus M, the cricket scorebook abbreviation for maiden over

explanation.surface: A rule about leaving a young woman out of one's prayers.
explanation.walkthrough: BEN(AM)E. A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored, abbreviated M.
explanation.definitionFit: Bename is an archaic verb meaning to name or mention, so it is a word no longer used for mention.

clue.text: Iceland makes legal claim — controversial matters

parts.note: IS is the international vehicle code for Iceland
one who makes a legal claim sues

explanation.surface: Iceland brings a lawsuit, raising disputed questions.
explanation.definitionFit: Issues are subjects of debate or dispute, points on which people disagree.

clue.text: Beans rinsed in kitchen sink once?

indicators.note: rinsed suggests being swilled around, so the letters are churned into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Beans being washed in the kitchen sink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' flags basen as an old Spenserian form of basin.
explanation.definitionFit: Basen is an obsolete spelling of basin, and a basin is the bowl of a kitchen sink.

clue.text: Scottish guards in mostly odd society

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the last letter of the word for odd is dropped

parts.note: weird means odd
S is the abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: Scottish soldiers on guard in a rather strange community.
explanation.walkthrough: WEIRD loses its D, then S. In Scots, to weir is to guard or ward off.
explanation.definitionFit: Weir is a Scots verb meaning to guard or defend, so weirs is the Scottish form of guards.

clue.text: Wood deity remains in this after fire?

definitions.text: Wood deity remains in this after fire?

parts.note: ash is a type of wood
Pan is the Greek god of the woods and shepherds

explanation.surface: A woodland god lingers in the fireplace after the fire burns out.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition as well as the wordplay: after a fire, ash is what remains in the tray.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashpan is the tray beneath a grate that collects the ash left once a fire has burnt.

clue.text: Son in difficulty makes comeback in game

indicators.note: a comeback is a return, so the assembled letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
taken as written
a net is a snare, a tangle one is caught in, hence a difficulty

explanation.surface: A son in trouble stages a revival in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: S + IN + NET gives SINNET, which read backwards is the game. NET for difficulty is loose: a net is something one gets caught up in.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis is a racket sport, a game played across a net.

clue.text: Cause of physical problem makes one endlessly irritable about hair

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shortened word goes around the word for hair
endlessly means with the end removed, so the last letter of the word for irritable goes

parts.note: sore can mean irritated or touchy
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Something wrong with one's body leaves one cross about one's hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' belongs with the link: the clue says the cause makes one, a person, irritable.
explanation.definitionFit: A stressor is any agent or stimulus that causes stress to an organism, a cause of physical or mental strain.

clue.text: "Ape", a term I'd fancy for ancestor of first authentic man?

indicators.note: to fancy here is to make something fanciful or invented, so the letters are rearranged into a new form

parts.note: the fodder, ten letters

explanation.surface: Someone suggests the word ape might suit a forebear of the first true human.
explanation.walkthrough: Adam is the first man of the Bible; a preadamite is a supposed human existing before Adam.
explanation.definitionFit: A preadamite is one held to have lived before Adam, the first man, so an ancestor of him, if such existed.

clue.text: Very old plan editor brought back later in Scotland

indicators.note: brought back means returned, so the abbreviation is written the other way round

parts.note: ED is the abbreviation for editor
syne is Scots for since or later, as in auld lang syne

explanation.surface: A long-standing scheme that the editor reintroduced later in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: ED reversed gives DE, then SYNE. 'Very old' marks desyne as an obsolete Spenserian spelling of design.
explanation.definitionFit: Desyne is an archaic spelling of design, and a design is a plan.

clue.text: Always, holy type suffering setback turns outwards

parts.note: ever means always

indicators.note: a setback here is being set back to front, so the abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint, a holy person

explanation.surface: A pious person who always suffers reverses ends up turning away.
explanation.walkthrough: EVER then ST reversed, TS.
explanation.definitionFit: To evert is to turn something inside out or outwards, as an eyelid can be everted.
